findings.title: Embedded-post username link lightness changed from 30% to 70% in light themes
findings.body: In the .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a rule, the original value was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), but the replacement uses dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The dark-theme branch (30%) follows the 70/30 inversion convention, but the light-theme value was silently changed from 30% to 70%, making usernames in reply expansions much lighter than before on light themes. The light value should stay 30%.

findings.title: group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The .user-stream .group-member-info .name rule changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). Per the convention used throughout this PR (light/dark values summing to 100%), the light-theme value should have remained 30% with a 70% dark counterpart, not been changed to 50%. Group member names become visibly lighter on light themes.

findings.title: Mobile group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Same as the desktop counterpart: .user-stream .group-member-info .name changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to a 50%/50% dark-light-choose pair. The light-theme value was unintentionally altered from 30% to 50%, deviating from the 70/30 inversion pattern applied to the adjacent .title rule (kept at 50% correctly). Group member names on mobile light themes lose their intended emphasis.

findings.title: custom-message-length light-theme lightness inverted (70% -> 30%)
findings.body: The .custom-message-length rule changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). The desktop version of the same rule (desktop/modal.scss) was converted to 70%/30%, preserving the original light-theme 70% value. The mobile conversion inverts the values, so the character-counter hint text becomes much darker on light themes and inconsistent with desktop.

findings.title: Topic map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: In .topic-map h3, the original scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) was replaced with dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). The equivalent desktop rule (desktop/topic-post.scss .topic-map h3) was correctly converted to 20%/80%. The mobile change silently alters the light-theme value from 20% to 50%, making the topic map heading noticeably lighter than before and inconsistent with desktop.
